# 314159265 (rank 16, 4.92 at 02:10:49 UTC): clean-room study and counter-tactics

Written 21 Nov 2026, about 07:40 UTC, by the clean-room analyst step (Opus). Read-only work: nothing from the
repository or the sandbox copy was executed, built or installed by me. Files were read with cat / grep / git show /
git diff only. No code, identifier, comment or constant table is reproduced; every number below is my own
description of behaviour read from the source at the scored commit. Short phrases from commit messages are quoted
as evidence only. Scratch scripts (timing checks, sim-log summary): tools/top10/pi_timing.py, pi_others.py,
pi_simstats.py, pi_kestrel_hashes.txt.

Repository: AbhirajTiwari12/mech-royale-bot (public, Python standard library, one 89 kB bot file plus a 474 kB
precomputed walk/height grid and an 88 kB list of 51 climbable roofs; 53 commits, 18:19-23:05 EST on 20 Nov =
23:19-04:05 UTC). Bot name announced to the server: "kestrel" (name only on the spectator stream; mechs are
anonymous in a match). Every commit carries an AI co-author line. No text aimed at AI agents or tools was found
(bot, tools, README, Dockerfile, ignore files and all 53 commit messages checked). No licence file.

## 0. The short answer

Two bots in one. In practice (no foreign deaths) it is a hostile-only skirmisher for the first 40 s and then a
no-retreat brawler: gun + laser at a 45 m ring, every visible mech inside 100-150 m is a target, it chases out of
sight and finishes the weak at 20 m. That earns 4.92, the same plateau as other no-retreat brawlers (Mahalas
5.15). In a free-for-all it latches on the first death it did not cause and becomes a skittish roof climber: any mech
seen inside 150 m makes it break off and walk to a roof up to 220 m away (or to cover 14-48 m away, boosting
whenever exposed), stand at the wall for up to 6 s collecting energy and jet up. That explains the recorded 41%
boosting, 36 s life and 12th average: it spends the opening in long, steady, undodged legs, standing still at wall
bases and rising slowly on jets, while ignoring every mech it does not consider hostile.

## 3. How it plays (G3, numbers read from the source)

Summary in ten sentences:
1. Match type: it starts in a cautious "opening" posture; a death it did not cause before 60 s, or a second such
   death at any time, latches free-for-all for good; at 40 s without a latch it switches to the practice posture.
2. Ranges by loadout: gun + laser holds 45 m (dead band 37-53 m), laser without gun 70 m, gun only 32 m, any
   lightning (with energy above 12) 24 m, and 75 m (with laser) or 58 m against a lightning carrier; a target under
   320 hp is closed to 20 m with boost when its own hp is above 40% and the target holds no lightning.
3. Engagement: a target is fought when inside 150 m (laser held) or 100 m (no laser), or 220 m if it was hit in
   the last 3 s; the gun fires only under 140 m, the laser charges on any line of fire inside about 270 m and is
   always released at full charge (0.69 s or more) with the aim on the target.
4. Retreat: in practice none at all after 40 s; in the opening it breaks off at 45% hp against one threat (unless
   winning), 70% against two within 150 m, 85% against three, and returns at 85%; in a free-for-all the same rule
   uses 60/80/90% with return at 90%.
5. Target rule: lowest of half the distance in metres + 0.09 x hp, +60 when out of sight, -15 for the current
   target and -25 for the mech that hit it in the last 3 s, so 1000 hp of difference weighs like 180 m: it switches
   to the weakest mech in reach.
6. Economy: weapons first (lightning worth about 1.5 cubes, laser 1.3, mortar 0.6 when a slot is empty), cubes,
   then ground crates (only with no mech within 180 m and hp at least 70%; in the opening and a free-for-all only
   hostile mechs count) and drones (hp above 60%), all
   discounted by distance + 25 m; mid-fight it scoops cubes within 30 m and detours for a laser or lightning within
   70 m (35 m if it already has one of them); calm supply drops within 260 m.
7. Loadout: an empty slot takes any wanted weapon (a mortar too when nothing else is held); in practice it then
   upgrades toward gun + laser, in a free-for-all toward laser + lightning (it drops the gun for lightning).
8. Upgrades: practice damage-first (laser damage, lightning efficiency, gun damage, gun rate, laser charge;
   plating only about eighth); free-for-all hull-first (plating, armour, nanites, then lightning efficiency, laser
   damage, servos).
9. Zone: keeps 22 m inside the current edge (more during a shrink: 14 s of edge travel ahead), heads for 55% of
   the next radius on its own side, boosts only when outside or within about 6 m (+4 m per m/s of edge speed) of the
   edge, and in the last circle walks to the centre and stands there.
10. Endgame: in practice nothing changes; in a free-for-all, at 3 or fewer alive, it stops running away and chases
   mechs it considers hostile.

Detail that matters for counters:
- Hostility (opening and free-for-all only; in practice everything visible is a target): a mech becomes hostile
  when it damages kestrel (20 s), closes faster than 4 m/s while aiming within 0.3 rad of it inside 170 m (15 s),
  is within 45 m with a line of sight (5 s), or charges a laser with its aim within 0.15 rad (15 s); in a
  free-for-all also when it is within 110 m in sight, under 35% hp and under kestrel's hp while kestrel is above 60%.
- Strafing: sideways direction re-drawn every 0.45-1.35 s with a 75% chance of reversal (mean about 1.2 s between
  reversals), an extra reversal when a gun bullet's closest approach in the next 0.45 s is under 3.5 m (no more
  often than every 0.35 s); with lightning and the target beyond 40 m it moves mostly radially and boosts in when
  energy is above 45 and the target is within 110 m. Bullet reversals and the charging-laser response exist only
  in this fight movement; retreat, roof, loot and zone legs have no dodge (mortar shells excepted: it steps away
  from a predicted landing within 15 m).
- Charging laser on its target: radial motion cut to 30%, full sideways weight, boost above 35 energy.
- Out of sight: when its target ducks behind cover within 60 m and it holds no lightning, it stops dead and holds
  the angle (it sidesteps only if hit in the last 2 s); farther away it paths after the target in the practice
  posture, and in the opening or a free-for-all only when it holds lightning and the target is within 90 m. In the
  middle of a free-for-all a lost sight line usually ends the fight instead (the hostile is no longer in sight inside 75 m, so it flees).
- Aim: gun leads with a first-order intercept plus 0.08 s; the laser aims at the target's position 0.1 s ahead;
  the gun fires when the aim is within about 2.4 m sideways and 3.5 m vertically of the lead point; the laser
  releases when within about 1.9 m sideways; it never pre-charges a target it cannot see (option off), and when it
  has nothing to shoot it spins its torso by commanding +1.2 rad per decision (it turns at the full 4 rad/s, a full
  turn in about 1.6 s) or, half of the time, snaps to a nearby sound.
- Peek (opening and free-for-all, two or more hostiles): searches spots on rings of 9-45 m where only its target
  can see it, at 70 m (laser) or 40 m (otherwise), 24 m with lightning against a target without lightning.
- Engineering: one Python process, a 6 ms budget per decision; path, cover, peek and roof searches are time-sliced
  by the wall clock (so the bot is not deterministic: a re-submission is a fresh draw); garbage collector off; a
  malformed message cannot kill it. Our sandbox smoke test: answers p50 0.3 ms, p99 2.2 ms, max 4.3 ms.

## 4. Why it scores (practice)

- Mechanism (my reading): practice points are house bots killed before we die. Kestrel arms and farms for 40 s
  fighting only mechs that shoot it, close on it while aiming, or come within 45 m, then fights everything in reach to the death with gun + laser at 45 m,
  where its own gun and laser are near-certain hits: about 100 damage per second sustained from the gun
  (12 rounds in 2.9 s, then 2.4 s reload) plus about 130 from full-charge beams every 2.4 s, boosted by cube
  scooping and damage-first upgrades, against a gun-only house bot dealing about 100. It focuses the weakest and
  finishes runners at 20 m. With no retreat, its life ends when 2-3 hunters converge, which caps it near 5.
- Its own logs: no number is published. The commit messages carry no scores; its simulator ("tuned so that known
  versions score roughly what the leaderboard gave them", house tiers easy to expert) prints scores but no result
  was committed. What the board allows, with care:
  - The 4.92 best stayed while the team pushed 23 playable candidates (H25, H60, R, K, BF, EC, EC10, EC10-K, PC,
    PB, five probes and re-rolls). With 4 submissions per rolling hour, at most about 8 of them could have been scored by
    04:05 UTC; each that was scored came in at or below 4.92. Upper bound only, per change: +0.00, unknown which.
  - Re-rolls: the same G3 play was recommitted under five more hashes (four labelled "fresh SHA") and EC10-K under
    three. Because the bot is clock-dependent, each submitted one is a new draw; if they were submitted (the label
    suggests so), none beat the first. Another team measured a spread of 0.23 for identical
    clock-dependent code (Doctrine D10). So 4.92 is probably near the top of G3's own spread; its mean is likely
    0.1-0.2 lower. [inference]
  - Their probes (passive after 120/180/240 s, after 4 kills) were measurements on the official scorer of when the
    points are earned; results not published.
- Official vs simulator: our uncalibrated simulator gave G3 6.0 in two smoke matches (places 10 and 10, 6 kills
  each, died at 58 s and 123 s, killed by a gun at 105 m and by lightning at 28 m with 7 hunters on it, 14 cubes,
  gun + laser) against 4.92 official; in the same smoke run the 5.58 bot got 7.5. Both inflated by 1-2 points,
  n = 2, no conclusion beyond "runs, no crashes, dies to converging hunters".

## 6. Limitations (each with its mechanism)

1. No retreat in the practice posture (and in a free-for-all window between 40 s and the first foreign death, if
   no mech died before 40 s): it fights to the death at 45 m, inside everyone's sure-hit range.
2. Laser telegraph and slowdown: it charges on every line of fire, moves at half speed (about 5.9 m/s) for 0.75 s
   of every 2.4 s, always waits for a full charge, never pre-charges out of sight, and without a line of fire lets
   the charge go after about 2 s.
3. Corner freeze: when its target ducks behind cover inside 60 m and it has no lightning, it stops dead and holds
   the angle until hit (practice posture, opening, last three alive, or when its target is weak prey; in mid
   free-for-all a lost sight line makes it flee instead).
4. Free-for-all skittish rule: any mech it has seen in the last 5 s inside 150 m (no line of sight needed) makes it
   break off, unless a hostile is in sight inside 75 m or the target is under 35% hp. It then
   heads for its home roof if one lies within 220 m (any roof inside the next circle within 260 m, 6-34 m high,
   median 18 m), walking and boosting only while energy is above 80, instead of the nearest cover; without a roof it
   runs to a spot 14-48 m away hidden from the nearest three mechs, boosting whenever one of them sees it and energy
   is above 8.
5. Roof climb: at the access point it waits up to 6 s, standing within 3 m of the wall, until energy reaches
   14 + 1.8 x roof height (46 for the median roof), pushes into the wall for up to 1.6 s, then jumps and jets
   straight up at no more than 10 m/s; two failed jets ban that roof for 90 s. On the roof it holds inner cells
   hidden from threats and fights only same-level mechs within 70 m, but keeps shooting at its target.
6. No dodging outside fight movement: retreat, roof, loot and zone legs are straight path segments at constant
   speed; an intercept aimer hits such movers about 84% of the time (Doctrine D1).
7. Narrow hostility: a mech that charges with its aim more than 0.15 rad off, closes slower than 4 m/s or with
   its aim more than 0.3 rad off, and stays beyond 45 m, is not hostile; kestrel's torso then follows someone else
   or spins, so that mech often hits its rear (x1.5).
8. Prey rush: a target under 320 hp without lightning draws a boosting, straight approach to 20 m (out of sight
   too, with energy above 50); in a free-for-all it also marks any mech under 35% hp within 110 m as prey when it
   is itself above 60%.
9. Weakest-first switching: 0.09 per hp against 0.5 per m and only 15 points of stickiness: a newly wounded mech
   in reach steals its aim mid-fight.
10. Idle spin: with nothing to shoot it turns at full rate; its weapons are off-target and a mech behind it needs
   up to 0.8 s of its turning before it can reply.
11. Mortar exposure: with a gun only and an empty slot it takes a mortar if that is the best pickup in reach,
   carrying cook-off risk (laser +60%) until a laser or lightning replaces it.
12. Last circle: walks to the centre and stands still there; no other endgame logic in practice.
13. Not deterministic: searches cut by the wall clock; under load its cover, peek and roof choices lag by several
   decisions.

## 7. Free-for-all behaviour (does the code explain 41% boosting, 36 s, 12th?)

Recorded: S4 (Achintya-Lakshmanan, up to 11 showdowns, 02:00-04:00 UTC) gives 41% of time boosting, about 36 s
alive, about 12th on average; S1/S3 have no per-team rows for it. All builds that could have played then (F1 from
01:09, G1, G2, G3) share the same free-for-all posture (I checked the profile at each), so the record describes
this posture. One difference in the opening: F1 and G1 (the builds before 02:00 UTC) had no cautious
opening, so from spawn until the first foreign death they played the practice brawler (no retreat, chase, 45 m);
G2 and G3 add the 40 s hostile-only opening ("better FFA start" in the G2 message).

From the code, the chain is:
1. 0 s to the first foreign death (median bottom-half death in showdowns is 21 s, so the latch usually comes in
   the first 10-20 s): cautious opening posture, walking to the best weapon, fighting only hostile mechs at its
   loadout ranges, retreating at 45/70/85%. Weapon detours inside a fight boost (energy above 40, more than 15 m).
2. After the latch: any mech within 150 m sends it to its roof (up to 220 m away) or to cover. Cover legs boost
   whenever a nearby mech has sight and energy is above 8 (a full tank lasts about 6 s; after that it re-boosts in
   short bursts every time energy creeps above 8); roof legs start with a boost while energy is above 80; the
   climb itself is 2-4 s of jets. Fights when a hostile is in sight inside 75 m add lightning approaches (boost above 45 energy) and prey
   rushes (boost above 40-50). In a crowded opening (bottom-half mechs had the nearest mech at 114 m on average),
   it is inside someone's 150 m almost all the time. So a boost share around 40% is what the code would produce.
   [inference, not replayed]
3. Why it dies early: straight, undodged legs (limitation 6), standing at a wall base for up to 6 s and rising
   slowly on jets (5), long walks to a roof instead of the nearest cover (4), breaking off fights it could win
   while non-hostile mechs get free side and rear shots (7), and a nearly empty tank when it arrives (no boost left
   to escape, no energy for the jet, so more standing).
4. Late game (rarely reached): on a roof inside the next circle; at 3 or fewer alive it chases hostile mechs; in
   the last circle it stands on the centre.
5. Expected in the final: the same, bottom half, usually dead by 60 s. Its own FFA tuning used lobbies of its own
   aggressive variants (8 aggressive + 7 cautious copies), which reward running away; real fields are calmer and
   laser-heavy, which punish long exposed legs.

## 8. Observable signatures (anonymous mech, a few seconds of watching)

- S1 Skittish break-off: within about a second of another mech coming inside 150 m (even without a sight line), it turns
  its legs away and heads for a building; its torso keeps tracking only a mech that shot it, aimed at it while
  closing, or came inside 45 m; otherwise it spins or snaps to sounds.
- S2 Wall-base wait then vertical jet: stops within 3 m of a building wall for up to 6 s (speed under 1 m/s), then
  pushes into the wall, jumps and rises at no more than 10 m/s onto a 6-34 m roof inside the next circle; it then
  sits on inner roof cells.
- S3 Idle torso spin at the full 4 rad/s (a full turn in about 1.6 s), or snaps toward a near sound.
- S4 Laser rhythm: `charging` whenever it has a line of fire and the cooldown is up; always 0.7-0.75 s charges;
  about 2.4 s per cycle; its speed halves while charging.
- S5 Fight ring when engaged: 45 m with gun + laser (practice posture), 70 m with laser and no gun (free-for-all
  loadout), 32 m gun only, 24 m lightning, 58-75 m from a lightning carrier, 20 m boosting rush on a target under
  320 hp; sideways reversals about every 1.2 s.
- S6 Corner freeze: stops dead when its target ducks out of sight inside 60 m (opening, the 40 s practice window,
  last three alive, or while hunting a target under 35% hp).
- S7 Loadout and hull: in a free-for-all ends laser + lightning (drops its gun when it finds lightning); max_hp steps
  1400 -> 1610 -> 1852 with the first offers (plating first).
- S8 Endgame switch: at 3 or fewer alive it begins to chase hostile mechs out of sight.

All gains are analytical estimates from the rules and its decision logic; none was measured.

| C4 | S6: after we break sight inside 60 m, the mech that was fighting us stops dead (speed under 1 m/s); expect it in the opening, at 3 or fewer alive, or when we are under 35% hp | Stay hidden, charge fully behind the corner (hold under 2 s), step out at most 3 m, release on the first decision with sight (stationary target), step back before 0.7 s; repeat every 2.4 s | 3 (corner freeze) and 2 (it needs 0.75 s of visible charge, never pre-charges out of sight) | About 315 for us per cycle against 1-2 of its bullets (45-90); two cycles push it below 60% and it retreats (free-for-all), three to four kill it in the practice posture | If the mech lists lightning it does not freeze (it paths in to 24 m and shorts our laser): then do not hold a charge inside 50 m, back off along cover (D11). | C5 | We are under 35% hp (or under 320 hp) and a mech above 60% hp within 110 m starts a straight boost (about 19.5 m/s) toward us; it holds no lightning | Stand behind cover with a full charge held and the gun ready; release as it comes into sight inside 30 m; keep facing it (front arc) | 8 (prey rush to 20 m; it does not break off while we hold under 60% of its hp and nobody else is close, and never in the practice posture) | Turns a likely death into a 20 m duel where our beam lands first: +1 place, sometimes a kill | Finishers with lightning (TTUN family closes to 28 m) short our laser: if the closer lists lightning, break sight instead. Medium |
| C6 | Final 3 or fewer alive and one survivor earlier showed S1/S2/S3 | Stay non-hostile to it: do not shoot it first, stay beyond 45 m, do not close faster than 4 m/s with our aim on it, keep hp above 35%; let it chase the third mech, then third-party the survivor (D11) | 7 and the endgame switch: it chases only mechs it considers hostile | +1 place when the other two trade | Not kestrel: a real hunter comes anyway; our D11 rules still cover that. Low |

## 10. What this study cannot settle

- Identity rests on one sub-2 s timing hit plus a behaviour description; a chance mech-bot commit falls in a given
  2 s window about 25% of the time, so a coincidence is not excluded (the milestone label and the behaviour match make
  it less likely).
- The 41% / 36 s / 12th record is from one team's report with no per-match rows, no definition of "boosting" and no
  version stamp; the explanation above is from code, not from a replay.
- Which later variants were actually submitted, and what the passive probes measured.
- Whether the team will pick G3 or EC10-K for the final (same free-for-all play) or push something new before the
  cutoff.
